response.sql: SELECT AVG(d.avg_duration) AS avg_of_avg_duration, AVG(d.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_duration, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) AS d;

assumptions.assumption: The database is MySQL, as the schema syntax (Sakila-style, with the YEAR type and inline KEY definitions) indicates. The CAST to DOUBLE avoids MySQL's DECIMAL division, which truncates to a fixed number of extra decimal places and would make the ratio less than exact.
Films with a NULL rating would form their own group. The schema allows NULL in film.rating, but the verified data shows only the five levels G, PG, PG-13, R and NC-17, so no such group should appear.
